problem_type: parallel HTTP onboarding ownership and premature completion semantics
symptom: Manual connection save, model registration, existing-model adaptation, future programmatic setup, task polling, and cancellation could enter Provider Adapter through separate actions; confirming models only wrote unverified rows while callbacks and copy treated registration as completion, and discovery assembled BaseURL candidates separately from production request construction.
direct_cause: Renderer/preload/IPC exposed register, start, register-existing, start-existing, and adapt-existing as sibling execution paths. ProviderAdapterService was both a reusable HTTP implementation and a public workflow owner, while model-list discovery maintained independent URL joining rules.
class_root: HTTP onboarding lacked one canonical certification boundary that owns start/get/cancel/promotion semantics and delegates all provider-specific discovery, compile, repair, verification, and request construction to shared primitives.
affected_population: Users saving a new HTTP API connection and assuming selected models were usable
Users adding or repairing models on an existing connection
Future Agent-driven sessions that would otherwise create a second certification workflow
Users whose BaseURL already contains /v1, /api/v3, no version segment, or a trailing slash
entry_points: New and existing model confirmation from ModelPickerScreen
Provider certification get/list/cancel/retry from the task workspace
Saved-connection model discovery and production request execution
internal_only_reason: The defect is Nomi's workflow ownership, persistence visibility, and callback semantics. External provider documentation cannot decide when Nomi may publish an unverified model or how Nomi's IPC paths converge.
invariants: ConnectionCertificationService is the only public HTTP certification start/get/cancel/list owner; manual and programmatic entry points produce the same canonical run shape.
HttpProviderConnector delegates Provider Adapter registration, discovery, compile, repair, verification, and lifecycle work without copying vendor/model branches.
A connection-only secure save produces configured/unverified disabled state and never starts, completes, or promotes a run.
Confirming one or more models starts one canonical certification run; selected rows remain invisible to production consumers until verified promotion commits.
One idempotency key and effective contract resolve to one child run regardless of whether the caller is manual UI or a programmatic session.
Manual IPC, preload, and renderer no longer expose direct register-existing or adapt-existing completion paths.
Discovery and production build concrete requests through buildHttpRequest, including /v1, /api/v3, unversioned, and trailing-slash BaseURLs.
Registration callbacks and localized copy never describe configured/unverified state as completed or usable.
migration: Existing verified active revisions remain usable. Existing configured/unverified rows remain visible only in settings and require a new canonical certification start. Renderer bridge and IPC channel names migrate in one change; removed direct register-existing/adapt-existing paths are not retained as fallbacks.
residual_risks: Task 6 will add the persistent programmatic session owner; Task 4 exposes the same canonical service API and verifies its shape without implementing MCP or session UI.
ComfyUI migration is intentionally deferred to Task 5 and remains outside this HTTP-only contract.
